question: Should OpenClaw extend the public Gateway command catalog with generic descriptionLocalizations now, or keep localized native-command metadata confined to the current owner-specific surfaces until a broader client contract is approved?
rationale: This choice establishes the long-lived command metadata boundary for Gateway, UI, channels, plugins, and generated SDK consumers; source inspection cannot determine the intended permanent product contract.

options.title: Approve a shared catalog contract
options.body: Confirm that generic localized descriptions belong in CommandEntry, document client fallback and compatibility expectations, and review the resulting SDK/protocol surface before merge.

options.title: Keep localization owner-specific for now
options.body: Remove the generic Gateway field and use the already-supported native-surface metadata path until a separately approved cross-client contract is ready.

options.title: Pause the localization series
options.body: Defer this cumulative architecture until the RFC and relevant command, Gateway, and plugin owners agree on a staged landing plan.

recommendation.title: Keep localization owner-specific for now
recommendation.body: Remove the generic Gateway field and use the already-supported native-surface metadata path until a separately approved cross-client contract is ready.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent command-surface documentation work covers the registry boundary and existing native command localization behavior affected by this decision.
